His writing has appeared in The New York Times, The Washington Post, The Atlantic, Slate, Defector, and Fast Company, among others. Deeply rooted in this nation's history and tradition, since 2021

title: Double V Ranch in eastern New Mexico lists for $35.2 million - Albuquerque Journal
content: Support local news. Please select your privacy preferences to continue. The property spans 73,600 acres, making it the state’s largest on the market right now The Double V Ranch may not be New Mexico’s largest ranch, but it is the largest ranch currently on the market. The 73,600-acre ranch, situated roughly 42 miles north of Roswell near Fort Sumner, hit the market for $35.2 million earlier this month. The brokers responsible for the listing are Brian Cook and Brannon Nash of Texas-based Phyllis Browning Co.’s Land and Ranch division. It is the company’s first listing beyond the borders of the Lone Star State. “There is a long-standing affinity between Texas and New Mexico, with many Texans owning homes, ranches and vacation properties throughout the state,” said Phyllis Browning CEO Jennifer Shemwell in a statement. “This expansion allows us to better serve clients seeking exceptional properties across a broader regional market.” Cook declined to identify the Double V Ranch’s owner, citing their desire for privacy, but said they are based out of Texas. Over the course of Cook’s seven-year real estate career and one year as managing director of Phyllis Browning’s Land and Ranch division, he said inquiries about land opportunities in New Mexico are common among his Texas clients, especially those in the cattle ranching and hunting industries. “There’s a lot of interest,” said Cook, who grew up visiting Santa Fe and went on hunting trips in New Mexico. “It’s a great market, it’s beautiful country, and so getting to be a part of the first steps into the state and bring something — especially of this magnitude — has been a fun experience.” The Double V Ranch’s vast open landscapes and water features make it ideal for cattle operations, which is what the property’s current owner used it for. In a good year, the ranch can facilitate an operation of up to about 1,200 cows and calves, Cook said he learned from the property’s ranch manager. “I don’t know exactly how many they have out there right now. Obviously, it’s a little dry, but that’s what the land can hold pretty conservatively,” Cook said. The existing cattle operation isn’t part of the ranch listing, Cook said, but the owner may be willing to continue their operation if a buyer wanted to lease the property back to them. The ranch’s physical structures are part of the package, including a four-bedroom, five-bathroom residence, several guest cottages, livestock facilities, sheds, fencing and even a historic saloon. Several interior roads span the property, part of which also borders N.M. 20. While New Mexico has been short of rain lately, Cook said water is still a prominent feature of the Double V Ranch. More than 25 miles of creeks and 1 mile of the Pecos River flow across the property. The ranch also has several water holes, springs and wells. Wildlife known to frequent the property include pronghorn antelope, mule deer, quail and seasonal waterfowl birds — making a minimal level of hunting another potential use for the property. Cook said the sheer volume of the Double V Ranch became fully apparent to him when he had the opportunity to tour it via helicopter earlier this year. “That was pretty remarkable to get to fly and truly see how much land and how much water was out there,” Cook said. The ranch’s availability has received significant interest since its June 4 listing. Cook said he’s been surprised to receive calls from interested parties all across the country, including Texas, New Mexico, Arizona, California, Oregon and Florida. “Opportunities like the Double V Ranch don’t come along often,” Cook said, touting the property’s rare combination of acreage, water access and diverse landscapes. The broker anticipates a quick sale but said his and the ranch owner’s ultimate goal is “to see land be conserved and preserved.” Kylie Garcia covers retail and real estate for the Journal. title: FSU’s Robert McCray V has signed an Exhibit 10 contract with the Los Angeles Lakers - 247Sports

title: 4 years after Roe v. Wade overturned, Red River Women’s Clinic launches new patient fund - Valley News Live
content: MOORHEAD, Minn. (Valley News Live) - Four years after the U.S. Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade and North Dakota’s trigger ban outlawed most abortions in the state, Red River Women’s Clinic (RRWC) has launched a new fund aimed at helping patients cover the costs of getting care. The independent clinic, now located in Moorhead, was North Dakota’s only abortion provider for more than 20 years when the court’s decision came down on June 24, 2022. Clinic Director, Tammi Kromenaker, said staff had just closed on their new building in Minnesota the afternoon before the ruling. “On June 24, 2022, Roe v. Wade was overturned. Obviously, it was devastating,” Kromenaker said. “There were three of us in the office that day, and the phone was ringing as normal.” When Roe was overturned, North Dakota’s trigger law banning most abortions was set to take effect. RRWC challenged the law in court while quietly preparing to move across the river to Minnesota, where abortion remains legal. Kromenaker said the team renovated the new space, moved more than two decades of records and equipment out of downtown Fargo and kept the Moorhead location largely under wraps because of security concerns — all while continuing to see patients. “It was an enormous amount of money that we literally did not have in order to move,” she said. To cover infrastructure costs tied to the move — including remodeling, security, and upgrades to the building — a local supporter started a GoFundMe with a goal of $25,000. The fundraiser quickly went viral. “It was honestly overwhelming, but just amazing to see the local community support, the regional support,” Kromenaker said. “And honestly, we heard from people as far away as Italy and France reaching out to us.” In the end, the GoFundMe raised more than $1 million dollars; money the clinic says helped it relocate without missing a single day of patient care. Now, on the near four-year anniversary of that campaign and the Roe decision, RRWC is explaining a new patient fund they rolled out in the spring called the Red River Clinic Fund. Unlike the earlier GoFundMe, which paid mostly for infrastructure and relocation costs, the new 501(c)(3) fund is designed to be patient-focused. Clinic leaders say it will help cover expenses such as professional interpreter services for non-English-speaking patients, travel costs for those coming from out of town, and small comforts like food and drinks on procedure days. “Each patient is going to present with a unique situation,” Kromenaker said. “And without having to ask permission from another fund — ‘can we cover this, can you get us a gift card’ — this new Red River Clinic Fund will allow us to say, ‘yes, you unique patient, you can have that unique thing that you need.’” The clinic says interpreter services in particular can cost thousands of dollars a year and are not typically covered by other abortion funds. Staff say they refuse to pass those costs on to patients. “We have plans to stay here,” the director said. “As long as patients in this region need our care, our plan is to deliver that care to them.” Both the original GoFundMe and the new Red River Clinic Fund are currently accepting donations. The clinic says it continues to face building needs, including a new roof and replacing an aging HVAC system.

title: Erling Haaland v Kylian Mbappé: how the Norway and France hitmen match up | World Cup 2026 - The Guardian
content:
Two of the best forwards in the game face each other in the World Cup on Friday. Their most dramatic contrast is in international football Golden Boot: World Cup 2026 top goalscorers
 All-time World Cup goalscorers Norway v France is arguably the most talent-loaded fixture in the World Cup group stage. Transfermarkt’s combined estimated market value of the two squads is higher than for any of the other 71 matches in this phase of the tournament. Yet the vast majority of the attention at Boston Stadium will be focused on just two men: Erling Haaland and Kylian Mbappé, who are already in the leading pack to win the World Cup Golden Boot for top goalscorers, both scoring twice in each of their first two games. They are very different types of forward. The Norwegian is the ultimate penalty area player, capable of finding space in the most dangerous spots where none appears to exist. His French counterpart is far more comfortable dribbling from wide areas, completing as many take-ons in two games as the Manchester City man does all season. Despite their contrasting styles, they have delivered near-identical output in Europe’s big five leagues since Haaland made his debut for Borussia Dortmund in January 2020. The similarities in their headline numbers are uncanny. Mbappé has made one more league appearance in that time, spending just 11 additional minutes on the field. Haaland leads the goal tally by two, Mbappé takes the assist battle by five and Harry Kane is the only man ahead of either of them once those two metrics are combined (for what are known as goal contributions). The England striker has played over 1,700 minutes more too. Haaland and Mbappé are a little further apart in the Champions League. Their playing time differs more here, thanks to the France forward representing teams that expect to compete for the continental crown from a younger age. Yet Haaland is the only one of the two who possesses a winner’s medal for the competition, with the data hinting at why that might be. The duo have similar rates of combined goals and assists per 90 minutes in the Champions League since Haaland’s debut, but Mbappé has been less effective in the knockout phase. It is their records in international football that will be most pertinent on Friday. Their goal tallies for their countries are just one apart. A more significant difference is that Mbappé has played almost twice as many such matches as Haaland, opening his goal account for France more three years earlier. With a stronger cast of colleagues behind him, Mbappé feels more likely to take the honours at Boston Stadium. Haaland should have more international goals once their careers have drawn to a close, though.

title: What Cletus Thinks About “Democracy” - The Bulwark
content: My best friend and I have a long-running dialogue about what The People want, and the nice part of this conversation is that we’re both right. Let me explain. When Sarah and I talk about “The People” we’re using shorthand for a subset of Trump voters that number in the tens of millions. Not the super-online edge lords. Not the captains of industry. Not the professional partisans. We’re talking about the folks who don’t have politics as part of their central identity. We’re talking about the “normal” people, out there in Red America, just living their lives and voting for Donald Trump. Cards on the table: I do not have a lot of sympathy for these folks. My thesis—especially since 2024—has been that they respond to Trump not in spite of his illiberalism, but because of it. My thesis is that they want the strongman stuff and everything else Trump offers them is beside the point. And as I said: We’re both right. If we’re talking about a group of, say, 40 million Americans (give or take), millions of them will be as I see them, and millions will be as Sarah sees them. But still, it can be useful to understand some of the currents of this group’s thought, even as we allow that there is no single, correct answer. Today we have something amazing: A big study in which researchers hunkered down with The People and had detailed conversations with them, over long periods of time. The study, sponsored by the Johns Hopkins Agora Institute and published in May, is here. Researchers embedded with folks in super-red counties in Wyoming, Michigan, and South Carolina. Here’s how they describe their methodology: This study relies on ethnographic research sustained immersion in people’s homes, lives, and communities through extensive interviews, observations, participation, and relationship-building. Where much democracy research documents what people say they believe, ethnography examines how and why political worldviews take shape within the full context of daily experiences, relationships, and social environments. . . . The ethnographic stance requires sustained curiosity and a commitment to deeply understanding people on their own terms. Our role as researchers is one of translation: to convey how independent and what some might see as “competing” beliefs make sense within the context of people’s lives. Pretty amazing, right? Now let me hit you with the big takeaway: 14 out of 21 participants in this study had an immediate negative reaction when asked about democracy. As a wise man once said: They are who we thought they were. I want to go deep on this question because the people in the study describe a remarkable consistency about why they dislike democracy. It’s not that they’re misled, or mistaken. They have a coherent worldview.

title: Can the 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 Raise the Bar for Premium Pickups Again? - MotorTrend
content: Bigger V-8s, bigger screens, and bigger ambitions for the Sierra lineup. The full-size pickup truck wars are real, and they are brutal. Into this fray, GM will introduce its next generation of trucks later this year: the bread-and-butter Chevrolet Silverado family for the masses and the premium GMC Sierra lineup for the more discerning. We already got our first look at what to expect from the 2027 Silverado 1500: a new look and a pair of new V-8 engines. So it should come as no surprise that the Sierras sport a new—but different from Chevy—look but the same powertrain lineup that includes new small-block V-8 engines among the four powertrain choices. So how does the 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 differentiate itself? GMC executives insist the Sierra buyer is a different animal, one who researches their purchase thoroughly and expects more in terms of looks, materials, amenities, and technology. 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 AT4 for those who go off-road. The current Sierra introduced the MultiPro tailgate with six distinct functions in 2018 as its whiz-bang feature to draw attention. Mike MacPhee, global vice president of Buick and GMC, says the tailgate has been enhanced with a lighter weight and more tie-downs. The new truck introduces innovations like an articulating infotainment screen that conceals a hidden storage cubby and a two-tiered center console. But the real difference is that the team took a strong truck and one-upped every aspect, from powertrains to tire size, digital displays, and the audio system. While the Silverado is offered in seven trims ranging from $45,195 to $74,595, the Sierra buyer will have six choices. The key trims are the Denali and AT4 brands, which have seen their relative volumes double over the past 10 years. The trim walk goes from Pro, to Elevation priced in the heart of the market, to AT4, Denali, and then AT4X and Denali Ultimate. In terms of design, the trucks needed to take a step forward, GM design director Holt Ware said. They have a more powerful stance with a raised hood to accommodate the larger engines and a raised vertical grille and front fenders to accentuate it. They sport signature LED headlights and taillights with an animated lighting dance. Quad exhaust tips are available. The bed has best-in-class volume, according to GM. The design team went for more differentiation between trims, too, with machined grilles and 22-inch wheels for Denalis while the raised AT4 gets a unique hood and wheels for better approach and departure angles. The AT4X is the most rugged expression with a 2-inch suspension lift, new fascia, 35-inch Goodyear Wrangler Territory MT tires, new Multimatic jounce bumpers (bump shocks) for high-speed impacts over the big stuff, and front and rear e-locking differentials. Inside, the emphasis is on nicer materials in cabs that have all been completely redesigned. The Denali Ultimate was designed to be cross-shopped against luxury sedans, with open-pore birch wood, a 16-speaker Bose premium audio system, heated and ventilated seats, and an available panoramic sunroof. It comes with three years of Super Cruise, the hands-free driver assistance system. The AT4 has mahogany wood trim, perforated patterns, piping, quilting, embroidery, enhanced bolstering on the seats, a sport flat-bottom steering wheel, and a standard panoramic sunroof. There are 60 inches of screen. The driver has a 12.2-inch split-screen display as well as a 15.0-inch head-up display. The star attraction is the I6.3-inch infotainment screen in the center, which articulates to reveal a hidden storage area tucked in behind while still offering a slimmer display. The passenger also has an 11.5-inch display with an articulating cover to hide it. This is a big upgrade from the current truck’s basic 7.0-inch and 13.4-inch touchscreens. 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 Ultimate Denali center console serves as work space. The new MultiPro center console is multi-tiered and opens to create an expanded work surface while making it easier to manage devices and gear. There are wireless chargers, a new steering wheel, hard and soft controls, and more storage overall. Like the 2027 Silverado 1500, the new Sierra goes on sale late this year with four powertrain options. The new 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter V-8s replace the 355-hp 5.3-liter and 420-hp 6.2-liter Gen V engines on the 2026 model. The sixth-generation small-block V-8 shares parts with the new LS6 6.7-liter V-8 engine on the Chevrolet Corvette Grand Sport, which delivers 535 hp and 520 lb-ft of torque. GMC is not yet providing specs for the Sierra. The larger-displacement engines have the power to tow and haul, accelerate quickly, and sound good doing it. The other engine choices include an enhanced 2.7-liter TurboMax I-4 and the 305-hp, 495 lb-ft Duramax 3.0-liter turbodiesel I-6 for efficiency and torque for towing and long hauls. All are mated to a 10-speed automatic transmission, including the I-4 that previously paired with an eight-speed. The engines will be built at GM factories in Flint, Michigan, Tonawanda, New York, and St. Catharines, Ontario. There are no plans for a hybrid. Executive chief engineer for full-size trucks and SUVs Mark Dickens says hybrids account for less than 1 percent of full-size pickup sales—although that number is expected to grow as more become available—and he says the diesel is a more efficient choice. Cargo box sizes remain the same as the previous-generation Sierra and include the 69.9-inch short bed, the 79.4-inch standard bed, and the 98.2-inch long bed. Availability of bed length depends on which cab you choose from among the usual single-, double-, and crew-cab configurations. GM builds full-size trucks in Indiana and Ontario and will add production in Michigan in 2027. The automaker sees the Sierra as a benchmark, a premium truck with full capability, strength, and refinement for the discerning customer who expects more. The Sierra is the highest-volume vehicle for the brand and the clearest expression of what it stands for. The truck had a record sales year in the U.S. in 2025 and gained market share. The Silverado and Sierra combined account for almost a third of GM’s sales in the U.S. GMC executives expect momentum to continue with the new model, noting higher gas prices have not impeded sales. “I think this is the truck against which all other trucks will be measured,” global marketing director for Buick and GMC Patrick Finnegan said. title: The 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 Rocks Three Screens on the Dash and More Technology than a Best Buy - Car and Driver
content:
GMC's bread-and-butter pickup is entering its next generation, which ushers in new V-8 options, more screen real estate, and interior and exterior redesigns. GMC's role within the overarching General Motors family is twofold. First, keep the Savana alive and unchanged until the heat death of the universe. Second, zhuzh up Chevy trucks and SUVs and sell them like hotcakes. The 2027 Sierra 1500 is finally here, and along with bringing the brand's most popular model into a new generation, it should do a lot to help with that second task. The new Sierra joins the fray a week after Chevrolet revealed the 2027 Silverado 1500, with changes to both trucks following the same pattern. The Sierra gets a new exterior design, an overhauled interior, new engines, and enough tech to make a Geek Squad employee dizzy. See all results for new 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 for sale near 85032 Comparing the 2027 Sierra to the previous model year, the new truck's fenders are more pronounced, the grille is larger and more upright, and the hood adds more contouring to make the whole truck appear more muscular. A new pair of headlights is set into the bulky fenders, with redesigned taillights flanking the updated MultiPro tailgate. Inside, the Sierra's dashboard-mounted screen real estate has grown for the new generation. The driver is now treated to a 12.2-inch digital gauge cluster, while the passenger is treated to an 11.5-inch screen with a closing cover. Both front occupants benefit from the new 16.3-inch center infotainment screen that lifts to reveal a hidden storage compartment. The center console has been updated too, with the MultiPro unit providing a workspace or access to cupholders and chargers. Apart from the two new V-8s, changes under the bodywork are a bit more restrained. The AT4X trim gets updated jounce control dampers from Multimatic and a new set of 35-inch Goodyear Wrangler Territory MT tires. But back to those new mills. The 2027 lineup arrives with GM's new 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter engines, which join the returning 2.7-liter turbocharged four-cylinder and the Duramax diesel 3.0-liter straight-six. title: GM reveals 2027 GMC Sierra pickup with new V-8 engines, redesigned styling - CNBC
content:
DETROIT – General Motors revealed its 2027 GMC Sierra 1500 pickup truck lineup on Thursday with new V-8 engine options and redesigned interior and exterior styling. The new GMC trucks are crucial to the automaker’s sales and earnings, especially the highly profitable Denali luxury models and off-road AT4 models that represent roughly half of the vehicle’s current sales, according to GM. Such models feature unique parts, accessories and amenities to boost pricing and profits for the company. GM said Thursday it’s narrowing its model lineup for the next-generation Sierra to the Pro, Elevation, AT4, AT4X, Denali and Denali Ultimate. It’s removing the mid-level SLE and SLT trims, which currently start at about $51,500 and $57,900, respectively. GM said pricing details as well as performance specifications will be released closer to when the vehicles go on sale late this year. Starting prices for the current Sierra 1500 lineup ranges from roughly $41,000 for an entry-level Pro to more than $86,000 for a Denali Ultimate. “With the next-generation Sierra 1500, we’re bringing together a new generation of Small Block V8 power, precise off-road capability, and our most immersive cabin experience to date,” said Michael MacPhee, vice president of GM’s GMC and Buick brands, in a release. “The next-generation Sierra is the truck all others will be measured against.” The new trucks come a week after the Detroit automaker unveiled updates to its Chevrolet Silverado 1500 pickup trucks, which are mechanical siblings to the GMC models. Most noticeably the GMC pickups are styled far differently than their Chevy brethren, including taking styling cues from the brand’s all-electric Sierra pickup truck and featuring a new interior. The interior cabin comes with more storage, a sliding center console and a folding table or work surface — all made possible by moving the gear shifter from the center console to behind the steering wheel. It also features new technologies and more than 60 inches of available screens, including an 11.5-inch passenger-side screen that includes media and entertainment functions. Other significant changes are found under the hood. Like the Silverado models, the GMC pickups will include a new generation of the automaker’s small block V-8 gas engines, available in 5.7-liter and 6.6-liter options. In addition to the V-8 engines, the GMC trucks will offer two six-cylinder engines, including a GM-exclusive diesel variant. GM’s U.S. sales through the first half of this year are forecast to decline by roughly 7%, according to Cox Automotive. The overall market is expected to see sales fall roughly 3%, Cox said Wednesday. GM reported first-quarter sales were down 9.7% compared with a year earlier, with its GMC brand about level. Sales of the Sierra 1500 were down about 2% to nearly 51,900 units, while larger, heavy-duty models were off about 8% to roughly 24,500 units. Sales of the electric Sierra were up 3%, but remained under 1,300 units. (DTN) -- A 73,600-acre cattle ranch hit the market in New Mexico with an asking price of $35.2 million and is advertised as the perfect fit for large-scale cow-calf operations. The Double V Ranch in De Baca County, New Mexico, features about 64,000 deeded acres and 9,600 acres of state land, located about 42 miles north of Roswell, New Mexico, according to a news release from Phyllis Browning Land and Ranch Company. The Double V Ranch includes a paved frontage along New Mexico State Highway 20 and additional county road access. The ranch features gently rolling terrain with productive bottomlands, multiple draws and elevations ranging from roughly 3,800 to over 4,250 feet. The ranch is home to more than 25 miles of creek frontage along Conejo Creek, Arroyo Mora and Arroyo Arana, in addition to one mile of Pecos River frontage, numerous permanent water holes, flowing springs and a strong well system. According to the realtor, the property is well improved with a four-bed, four-bath foreman's home, multiple guest houses, livestock facilities, barns and extensive fencing and interior roads. "In addition to its agricultural productivity, the ranch offers recreational value with hunting opportunities for antelope, deer, quail and seasonal waterfowl," the company said in a news release. Improvements to the ranch include a large metal hay shed, multiple equipment barns and usable outbuildings. The ranch is fenced and cross-fenced into 18 pastures. The property comes equipped with a large set of working pens, complete with scales, and several smaller sets of pens across the property. The Double V Ranch gained regional news attention in May 2013 during a severe drought. On May 17, 2013, New Mexico Livestock Board officials executed a search warrant at the ranch and discovered at least 25 dead cattle and about 1,000 emaciated animals at risk of starvation. Former ranch owner Richard Evans was charged with 25 counts of cruelty to animals. Later that month, a judge agreed to allow Evans to sell the herd to a buyer in Pampa, Texas, rather than proceed with a forced seizure. While the Double V Ranch is large, it is small in comparison to the largest ranches in the state, including Singleton Ranches, which includes 937,950 deeded acres as the state's largest. The second-largest ranch in New Mexico is the Vermejo Park Ranch at 558,000 deeded acres owned by the late Ted Turner. "Opportunities like the Double V Ranch don't come along often," Phyllis Browning Land and Ranch Managing Director Brian Cook said in a news release. "This is an incredible property with everything needed for a successful large-scale ranching operation. It's uncommon to come across a place with this much acreage, significant water access and diverse landscapes all in one." The Double V Ranch is well known for its variety of wildlife, including pronghorn antelope, mule deer and quail, as well as seasonal waterfowl. title: World Cup schedule today: How to watch Turkey v USA, TV channels & live stream Thursday 25 June - The Guardian
content: Live blog: the latest news from around the tournament So far, so good for the USA, who have already secured their spot in the World Cup knockout rounds as group winners after wins over Paraguay and Australia. Mauricio Pochettino and his players could be forgiven for easing their foot off the pedal for Thursday’s return to Los Angeles to face Turkey. Indeed, Pochettino may choose to rest some of his best players and ease Christian Pulisic back into action after injury. The USMNT head coach wants competition within his squad and Thursday’s match against Turkey may be useful to foster that before the matches that really matter. Elsewhere, Ecuador need a win over Germany to stand any realistic chance of making the last 32 while Sweden take on Japan looking to bounce back from their 5-1 humbling at the hands of the Netherlands. Here is your complete guide on how to watch today’s World Cup games, including kick-off times, broadcast networks and online streaming options. Curaçao’s historic draw with Ecuador kept alive their slim chances of making it out of Group E. Dick Advocaat’s side now aim to frustrate Côte d’Ivoire in a similar way. The Blue Wave have been one of the stories of this World Cup so far and a win would all but certainly keep it going into the knockout rounds. Côte d’Ivoire were made to rue Germany’s comeback from 1-0 down in their previous match, but still have still demonstrated enough in their two outings at this World Cup to suggest they could be a factor beyond the group stage. Their attacking talent in particular makes them a threat. Player to watch: Yan Diomande, Côte d’Ivoire – The RB Leipzig winger has been one of the most electrifying players at this World Cup with several of Europe’s biggest clubs lining up to sign him this summer. While Ecuador entered the World Cup as dark horses, they have so far failed to live up to their pre-tournament billing. Indeed, Sebastian Beccacece’s team have struggled for firepower in the final third and are still searching for their first goal. Now would be a good time for them to find their finishing instincts. Germany weren’t at their best against Côte d’Ivoire, but still had enough on their bench to turn around the game and make it two wins from two matches. Julian Nagelsmann has to prove his team have the right balance to win the World Cup for a record-equaling fifth time. Player to watch: Felix Nmecha, Germany – With a goal and an assist from two games, Nmecha has established himself as a starting figure in Germany’s midfield double pivot. His energy and willingness to play forward have been very valuable. Japan are flying under the radar as one of the most quietly impressive teams at this World Cup so far. Indeed, Hajime Moriyasu’s side swept aside Tunisia with ease after controlling large periods of their opening match against the Netherlands. They will use this final group game to tune up for the knockout rounds. Sweden’s strengths and weaknesses have been highlighted for all to see. They became the first side in World Cup history to lose their second match by a four-goal margin after winning their first match by a four-goal margin. Graham Potter’s outfit need more control. Player to watch: Alexander Isak, Sweden – The Liverpool forward has looked something like his old self at this World Cup and could be a difference-maker if Potter can find the right system to harness him without destabilising the rest of the team. Tunisia won’t have fond memories of the 2026 World Cup. Already out of the tournament after defeats to Sweden and Japan, the first of which prompted the firing of Sabri Lamouchi and Herve Renard’s hiring in his place, the African outfit have arguably been the worst team in the entire tournament. Fresh from putting five past Sweden, the Netherlands could be set for another big win. Not always known for their attacking prowess under Ronald Koeman, the Dutch may have found the right balance in the forward line after introducing Brian Brobbey as a focal point in their last match. Player to watch: Brian Brobbey, Netherlands – The Sunderland striker was too much for Sweden to handle and played an important role in bringing others into the game as well as scoring two goals of his own. Paraguay produced a gutsy performance to beat Turkey despite playing the second half with 10 men after Miguel Almiron’s red card. A draw for Gustavo Alfaro’s side will all but secure their place in the last 32 although a narrow loss could also be enough to carry the South Americans out of Group D. While Australia were kept at arm’s length by the USMNT in Seattle, their strength in defence and threat on the break, as demonstrated in the 2-0 win over Turkey, could give them an advantage in their final group fixture. Tony Popovic’s team have outperformed pre-tournament expectations. Player to watch: Nestory Irankunda, Australia – The Watford attacker was a dagger through Turkey’s heart in Australia’s opening fixture and could be the threat in quick transition that gives the Socceroos another impressive result. Few teams have progressed through their opening two matches of this World Cup more comfortably than the USA. On paper, Thursday’s encounter with Turkey looked to be their biggest test when Group D was drawn. With Turkey already out, though, it’s unclear what this match will hold. Turkey’s early elimination from the tournament was a shock, especially considering Vincenzo Montella’s team are ranked 11th out of 48 sides for expected goals (xG) and 10th for big chances created. They could take out some pent-up anger on the co-hosts in Los Angeles before heading home. Player to watch: Ricardo Pepi, USA – Pochettino could rotate his lineup for a dead-rubber and start Ricardo Pepi, giving the PSV forward an opportunity to make his mark and prove why he should be ahead of Folarin Balogun in the pecking order.

title: Wales v Barbarians: Sean Lynn names five uncapped Welsh players for non-capped international - BBC
content: Amy Williams has played for Brython Thunder and Wales Under-21s Five players will make their senior debuts for Wales when they take on the Barbarians at Allianz Stadium on Saturday (17:00 BST). Amy Williams and Kelsie Webster are named in the starting backline, while Stella Orrin, Lucy Isaac and Lily Hawkins are among the replacements. Kayleigh Powell, who shone at full-back during the Six Nations, gets an opportunity at fly-half, with Lleucu George among a host of Premiership Women's Rugby (PWR) players either rested or unavailable for the uncapped fixture. Seren Lockwood gets the nod ahead of Keira Bevan at scrum-half, while a fit-again Nel Metcalfe starts at 15. Metcalfe's youngster sister Branwen forms part of a strong-looking pack, which features the experience of Sisilia Tuipulotu, Alisha Joyce, Bryonie King and returning captain Alex Callender, along with Wales' rising star Jorja Aiono. The game in Twickenham is the second part of a double-header with Wales men facing the Baa-baas at 14:00 BST. "Somebody told me there are 11 under 22s in the squad and why not? We're talking about the next generation. I'm talking about 2029 [the next World Cup] and these individuals. "I want us as coaches having evidence, but also I'm giving them some experience into the international arena. There is no place in the matchday 23 for prop Jenni Scoble, who announced this week that she would hang up her international boots this weekend after struggling to balance a full-time career as a firefighter with the demands of professional rugby. Wales head into the game looking to end a nine-match losing streak, and centre Courtney Keight says it is important they do not get drawn into the Barbarians' open style of play. "The Baa-baas definitely play with flair so we have to stick to our processes, we're a very process driven team defensively and in attack so it's trying not to get caught up in the occasion," said Keight. "These are the kind of things you dream of when you play rugby. It's the big occasions, the big stadiums, double-headers with the men. "It's just so exciting, especially for some of the young ones coming through. It's just the pinnacle in your career sometimes to play in games like this." Wales' next generation getting a taste of Test life Carys Phillips is one of Wales' most capped players with 87 appearances Wales hooker Carys Phillips will create a bit of history when she lines up in the Barbarians side. She will be following in the footsteps of her father Rowland and the pair will become the first father-daughter duo to play for the Barbarians. New Zealand star Ruby Tui lines up on the wing in a squad that represents nine different nations and will be captained by Australia forward Emily Chancellor. "It's been a brilliant week in the heat, and we have been blessed with a wonderful group of people who have bonded amazingly in a short amount of time," said Barbarians women's head coach Susie Appleby. "Everyone will make a massive contribution on Saturday, and no doubt it will be a great occasion against Wales." title: Poland buys V-BAT drones to boost Baltic Sea naval operations - Defense News
content: WARSAW, Poland — The Polish Ministry of National Defence has awarded a contract to U.S. California-based defense technology firm Shield AI to buy its V-BAT drone for Poland’s Navy. The development comes shortly after Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced the company has offered Poland a role in its X-BAT autonomous vertical-takeoff fighter jet program, including some of the manufacturing activities for the craft. Shield AI said in a statement that the V-BAT will be deployed aboard a Polish Navy vessel, ensuring maritime domain awareness and intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) support to the force. “V-BAT has proven its capabilities in Ukraine and beyond, particularly in environments where communications and GPS links are disrupted or denied,” Ryan Tseng, Shield AI’s president, co-founder and chief strategy officer, was quoted in the statement. “Operations in the Baltic Sea, where security threats against critical energy and communications infrastructure are becoming more frequent, demand reliable sensor platforms and systems in all-weather conditions and sea states.” The Armament Agency, the Polish ministry’s procurement arm, said in a statement that “the delivery of the system, which comprises several platforms, is planned for later in 2026.” The deal puts Poland in line to become the first country on NATO’s eastern flank to acquire the drone. Warsaw will join other operators, including Greece and the Netherlands, as well as the U.S. Navy and the Japan Maritime Self Defence Force, according to data from Shield AI. “In addition to the aircraft themselves, the V-BAT system comes with ground control stations, antennas, spares, and maintenance equipment, and other operating equipment needed to maintain operational readiness,” a spokesperson for Shield AI told Defense News. The spokesperson said that “Shield AI is actively pursuing partnerships with Polish industry to support future autonomy, aviation, and defense programs. We look forward to expanding our engagement with Poland and sharing additional details in the coming months.” Since 2025, when Poland launched the Drone Force, its latest military component, the country has accelerated purchases of various classes of unmanned systems. Last month, the nation also joined the Pentagon’s counter-drone initiative to gain access to a marketplace that connects partner countries with emerging technology suppliers. Jaroslaw Adamowski is the Poland correspondent for Defense News.
